analyst_view.overall: Early view: Mallorca have not played since beating Cádiz 2-1 on 2 November, because their trip to Andorra was postponed, so Luis García's side arrive rested and sixth with a game in hand. Córdoba under Iván Ania have one defeat in their last five league games and beat Ceuta 3-0 last weekend, but finished the game before that, at Celta Fortuna, with nine men. Adrián Fuentes, Segunda's top scorer for much of the autumn, is Mallorca's main threat.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.5 goals. I lean slightly higher: Córdoba have scored in each of their last four league games (1-0, 2-0, 2-2, 3-0) and Mallorca's last two home games produced four and three goals. Fuentes is in form and Mallorca are fresh after a two-week gap.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.1 corners. I lean a little higher: Córdoba build a lot of their attacks through crosses (Fran Escribá asked Valladolid for aggression specifically to stop them), which earns corners even away, and Mallorca will have plenty of the ball at Son Moix.

cards.text: The numbers say 6.1 cards. I lean a touch higher: Córdoba ended the Celta Fortuna game with nine men after Álex Martín's straight red and Isma Ruiz's second yellow, a side that can lose its discipline when under pressure. With no referee named yet, I would not go far above six.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.3 shots and I leave it there. Mallorca at home and Córdoba's cross-heavy approach both produce attempts, but Mallorca's habit of drawing games (four draws in 12) suggests they are not always dominant. Nothing in the news moves the figure clearly.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.9 shots on target, which fits two sides with reliable finishers in Fuentes and Eder García. Mallorca's long break could mean fresh legs or a slow start, so I lean neither way.
